newsitem.title: UK: Morrison directors considering share sale.
newsitem.headline: Morrison directors considering share sale.

text.p: Morrison Construction Group Plc said on Tuesday that certain directors and senior executives are considering offering a limited number of shares for sale on the market.

The directors, including chairman Fraser Morrison and Gordon Morrison, who together with their immediate families hold 65.9 percent of the issued share, are considering making available up to one fifth of their current holding.
Fraser Morrison said that since the company's flotation in October 1995 a number of approaches have been made enquiring about further shares being made available.

He said that also, with a high proportion of equity held by the Morrison family directors and senior executives, the market for the group's shares was "less liquid than the company and its shareholders would like".

"This proposed sale will ease that situation and at the same time offer others the opportunity to participate in the further progress that we confidently look forward to as detailed in today's announcement of our latest annual results," chairman Fraser Morrison said in a statement.

The group announced a 42 percent jump in pre-tax profits for the year to March 31, 1997 to 16.2 million stg. It recommended a final dividend of 3.5 pence per share, making a total dividend of 5.14 pence, up 12 percent from the previous year's notional figure.
